claim: The Drosophila ventral nerve cord (VNC) receives and processes descending signals from the brain to produce a variety of coordinated locomotor outputs.
source: The Drosophila ventral nerve cord (VNC) receives and processes descending signals from the brain to produce a variety of coordinated locomotor outputs.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the function of the VNC.

claim: The VNC integrates sensory information from the periphery and sends ascending signals to the brain.
source: It also integrates sensory information from the periphery and sends ascending signals to the brain.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing VNC function.

claim: Single-cell transcriptomics was used to generate an unbiased classification of cellular diversity in the VNC of five-day old adult flies.
source: We used single-cell transcriptomics to generate an unbiased classification of cellular diversity in the VNC of five-day old adult flies.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the methodology.

claim: An atlas of 26,000 high-quality cells was produced, representing more than 100 transcriptionally distinct cell types.
source: We produced an atlas of 26,000 high-quality cells, representing more than 100 transcriptionally distinct cell types.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the data generated.

claim: The predominant gene signatures defining neuronal cell types reflect shared developmental histories based on the neuroblast from which cells were derived, as well as their birth order.
source: The predominant gene signatures defining neuronal cell types reflect shared developmental histories based on the neuroblast from which cells were derived, as well as their birth order.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing findings from the data analysis.

claim: The relative position of cells along the anterior-posterior axis could be assigned using adult Hox gene expression.
source: The relative position of cells along the anterior-posterior axis could also be assigned using adult Hox gene expression.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing findings from the data analysis.

claim: The adult Drosophila central nervous system (CNS) consists of the brain in the head capsule and the ventral nerve cord (VNC; also known as ventral nervous system) in the thorax.
source: The adult Drosophila central nervous system (CNS) consists of the brain in the head capsule and the ventral nerve cord (VNC; also known as ventral nervous system) in the thorax (Court et al., 2017; Ito et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The VNC receives and integrates sensory input from the periphery and sends this information to the brain in ascending neurons through the cervical connective.
source: The VNC receives and integrates sensory input from the periphery and sends this information to the brain in ascending neurons through the cervical connective (Tsubouchi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The brain sends sensory-motor signals to the VNC via descending neurons.
source: The brain, in turn, sends sensory-motor signals to the VNC via descending neurons (Namiki et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The VNC transforms signals from the brain into locomotor actions.
source: The VNC transforms these signals into locomotor actions (Harris et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The VNC controls muscles in the thorax in unique ways, depending on whether it is steering the wings during flight or generating acoustic communication signals during both reproductive and agonistic behaviors.
source: It controls muscles in the thorax in unique ways, depending on whether it is steering the wings during flight or generating acoustic communication signals during both reproductive and agonistic behaviors (Clyne and Miesenböck, 2008; Jonsson et al., 2011; Shirangi et al., 2013; von Philipsborn et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The VNC coordinates muscles in the legs to walk, jump, groom, reach, touch, and taste.
source: It coordinates muscles in the legs to walk, jump, groom, reach, touch, and taste (Bidaye et al., 2014; Card and Dickinson, 2008; Chen et al., 2018; Gowda et al., 2018; Harris et al., 2015; Howard et al., 2019; Kim et al., 2017; Mamiya et al., 2018; Mendes et al., 2013; Mendes et al., 2014; Seeds et al., 2014; Tuthill and Wilson, 2016; Wosnitza et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The VNC controls musculature in the abdomen relevant to copulation and reproduction including abdominal bending, attachment, and ejaculation in the male.
source: The VNC also controls musculature in the abdomen relevant to copulation and reproduction including abdominal bending, attachment, and ejaculation in the male (Crickmore and Vosshall, 2013; Jois et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2011; Pavlou et al., 2016; Tayler et al., 2012), and sperm storage and oviposition in the female (Kimura et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The VNC controls musculature in the abdomen relevant to sperm storage and oviposition in the female.
source: The VNC also controls musculature in the abdomen relevant to copulation and reproduction including abdominal bending, attachment, and ejaculation in the male (Crickmore and Vosshall, 2013; Jois et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2011; Pavlou et al., 2016; Tayler et al., 2012), and sperm storage and oviposition in the female (Kimura et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: Different functions of the VNC are orchestrated by anatomically discrete segments.
source: These different functions are orchestrated by anatomically discrete segments of the VNC.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: The thoracic neuromeres control the legs and wings.
source: Whereas the thoracic neuromeres control the legs and wings, the abdominal neuromere controls the abdominal muscles, gastric system, and reproductive organs.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: The abdominal neuromere controls the abdominal muscles, gastric system, and reproductive organs.
source: Whereas the thoracic neuromeres control the legs and wings, the abdominal neuromere controls the abdominal muscles, gastric system, and reproductive organs.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: Much of the developmental mechanisms that generate and assemble the VNC have been characterized.
source: Much of the developmental mechanisms that generate and assemble the VNC have been characterized (Venkatasubramanian and Mann, 2019).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: Drosophila undergo two stages of neurogenesis building two distinct nervous systems.
source: Like other holometabolous insects, Drosophila undergo two stages of neurogenesis building two distinct nervous systems.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: Embryonic neurogenesis gives rise to the larval nervous system.
source: Embryonic neurogenesis gives rise to the larval nervous system, and post-embryonic neurogenesis produces adult specific neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: Post-embryonic neurogenesis produces adult specific neurons.
source: Embryonic neurogenesis gives rise to the larval nervous system, and post-embryonic neurogenesis produces adult specific neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: The structure of the adult nervous system is established in the embryo where pioneering neurons setup networks of tracts, which later developing neurons follow.
source: The structure of the adult nervous system is established in the embryo where pioneering neurons setup networks of tracts, which later developing neurons follow (Hartenstein, 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The adult VNC is comprised of 4 primary neuromeres, three thoracic (one per each pair of legs: the prothoracic neuromere, ProNm; mesothoracic neuromere, MesoNm and metathoracic neuromere, MetaNm) and one fused abdominal neuromere (ANm).
source: The adult VNC is comprised of 4 primary neuromeres, three thoracic (one per each pair of legs: the prothoracic neuromere, ProNm; mesothoracic neuromere, MesoNm and metathoracic neuromere, MetaNm) and one fused abdominal neuromere (ANm) (Court et al., 2017; Niven et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The neuromeres, composed of one or more fused neuropils, are segment-specific parts of the CNS which process sensory signals and control movements of their specific segments.
source: The neuromeres, composed of one or more fused neuropils, are segment-specific parts of the CNS which process sensory signals and control movements of their specific segments.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: The thoracic neuromeres are homologous structures and are thus morphologically similar to each other.
source: The thoracic neuromeres are homologous structures and are thus morphologically similar to each other (Smarandache-Wellmann, 2016).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The neurons in the thoracic segments are derived from a set of repeating type I neuroblasts.
source: The neurons in these segments are derived from a set of repeating type I neuroblasts.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: Cells derived from a given neuroblast produce a lineage, which can be split into Notch+ and Notch- hemilineages.
source: Cells derived from a given neuroblast produce a lineage, which can be split into Notch+ and Notch- hemilineages (Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: The formation of tagmatic boundaries, which group segments into morphological units along the body axis, is established through differential expression of Hox family transcription factors (TFs).
source: The formation of tagmatic boundaries, which group these segments into morphological units along the body axis, is established through differential expression of Hox family transcription factors (TFs) (Angelini and Kaufman, 2005).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction with citation support.

claim: Cell types within each neuromere are genetically encoded by developmental programs.
source: Cell types within each neuromere are genetically encoded by developmental programs.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: It is unclear whether the mature terminal identity of an individual neuron can be determined from its adult transcriptome.
source: However, it is unclear whether the mature terminal identity of an individual neuron can be determined from its adult transcriptome.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: It is unknown whether the TFs involved in establishing the cellular diversity of the nervous system also play a role in the form and function of these same neurons in the adult.
source: It is for example unknown whether the TFs involved in establishing the cellular diversity of the nervous system also play a role in the form and function of these same neurons in the adult.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: The identity of a terminally differentiated neuron is likely to remain stable throughout the animal's life.
source: Although certain features of individual neurons can be plastic, the identity of a terminally differentiated neuron is likely to remain stable throughout the animal's life.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing was used to characterize the transcriptomes of individual cells in a 5 day old adult Drosophila VNC.
source: Here we used single-cell RNA-sequencing to characterize the transcriptomes of individual cells in a 5 day old adult Drosophila VNC.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction describing the methodology.

claim: An atlas of the VNC with 26,768 single-cell transcriptional profiles was generated that define more than 100 cell types.
source: We generated an atlas of the VNC with 26,768 single-cell transcriptional profiles that define more than 100 cell types.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction describing the data generated.

claim: The VNC has a roughly equal number of inhibitory GABAergic neurons and excitatory cholinergic neurons.
source: This analysis reveals that the VNC has a roughly equal number of inhibitory GABAergic neurons and excitatory cholinergic neurons, and that genes encoding preproneuropeptides are amongst the most highly expressed.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction describing findings from the data analysis.

claim: Genes encoding preproneuropeptides are amongst the most highly expressed in the VNC.
source: This analysis reveals that the VNC has a roughly equal number of inhibitory GABAergic neurons and excitatory cholinergic neurons, and that genes encoding preproneuropeptides are amongst the most highly expressed.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction describing findings from the data analysis.

claim: The segmentally repeating nature and developmental history of the VNC is born out in the cellular transcriptomes, as maintained expression of Hox and several other neuronal lineage marker genes persist.
source: The segmentally repeating nature and developmental history of the VNC is born out in the cellular transcriptomes, as maintained expression of Hox and several other neuronal lineage marker genes persist.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction describing findings from the data analysis.

claim: The single-cell profiles provide many novel markers for known and new cell types.
source: In addition, these profiles provide many novel markers for known and new cell types.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction describing findings from the data analysis.

claim: 80 VNCs were processed, 20 per independent replicate.
source: We processed 80 VNCs, 20 per independent replicate (Figure 1A; see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results describing the methodology.

claim: 26,768 high quality cells were recovered with a median of 1170 genes and 2497 transcripts per cell.
source: Pooling the data, we recovered 26,768 high quality cells with a median of 1170 genes and 2497 transcripts per cell.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results describing the data generated.

claim: The filtered single-cell data showed high correlation (r = 0.76) to FlyAtlas' bulk VNC sequencing data.
source: The filtered single-cell data showed high correlation (r = 0.76) to FlyAtlas' bulk VNC sequencing data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D; Leader et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing data validation.

claim: Comparisons of the pseudo-bulk expression levels between replicates of the filtered cells yielded correlations coefficients from 0.93 to 0.95.
source: Comparisons of the pseudo-bulk expression levels between replicates of the filtered cells yielded correlations coefficients from 0.93 to 0.95 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing data validation.

claim: A cluster resolution of 12 was chosen as it best resolved established substructures within the data.
source: A cluster resolution of 12 was chosen as it best resolved established substructures within our data (as described below).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results describing the data analysis methodology.

claim: The cluster resolution of 12 resulted in 120 distinct clusters.
source: This resulted in 120 distinct clusters (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing the data analysis results.

claim: Cells from independent experimental replicates were proportionally distributed across the clusters with an alignment metric of 94.6%.
source: Cells from independent experimental replicates were proportionally distributed across the clusters with an alignment metric of 94.6% (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A,B).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing data validation.

claim: All replicates contributed to all clusters (with one exception) and showed high correlation of cluster level expression.
source: All replicates contributed to all clusters (with one exception) and showed high correlation of cluster level expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing data validation.

claim: Replicate one did not have any constituents in cluster 118, which had only 22 cells total.
source: Replicate one did not have any constituents in cluster 118, which had only 22 cells total.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results describing the data.

claim: The 26,768 cells represent an approximate 1.5x coverage of the adult VNC.
source: These 26,768 cells represent an approximate 1.5x coverage of the adult VNC.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results describing the data coverage.

claim: Lineage based counts of the adult specific post-embryonic neurons in the VNC range from 10,000 to 11,000 cells.
source: Lineage based counts of the adult specific post-embryonic neurons in the VNC range from 10,000 to 11,000 cells (Birkholz et al., 2015; Lacin et al., 2019), with a total number of cells in the VNC forecasted to be ~16,000 (Lacin et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with citation support.

claim: The total number of cells in the VNC is forecasted to be ~16,000.
source: Lineage based counts of the adult specific post-embryonic neurons in the VNC range from 10,000 to 11,000 cells (Birkholz et al., 2015; Lacin et al., 2019), with a total number of cells in the VNC forecasted to be ~16,000 (Lacin et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with citation support.

claim: Connectomic analyses of the adult VNC using electron microscopy estimated a larger total number of ~20,000 cells.
source: Connectomic analyses of the adult VNC using electron microscopy estimated a larger total number of ~20,000 cells (Bates et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with citation support.

claim: Based on prior cell count numbers, the cell atlas has 1.3–1.7x coverage of the VNC.
source: Based on these prior numbers, our cell atlas has 1.3–1.7x coverage of the VNC.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results describing the data coverage based on inference from prior studies.

claim: 110 neuronal clusters were defined using expression of known neuron-specific and neuron-enriched genes.
source: We defined 110 neuronal clusters using expression of known neuron-specific and neuron-enriched genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 7; see methods), such as embryonic lethal abnormal vision (elav), neuronal Synaptobrevin (nSyb) and the long non-coding (lnc) RNA noe (noe) (Davie et al., 2018; DiAntonio et al., 1993; Kim et al., 1998; Robinow et al., 1988).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure and citations, describing the data analysis.

claim: These neuronal clusters can be distinguished from each other by differential expression of 1205 additional cluster markers.
source: These neuronal clusters can be distinguished from each other by differential expression of 1205 additional cluster markers (Figure 1D, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing the data analysis.

claim: Functional enrichment analysis of cluster-defining marker genes identified those encoding immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domains as most significantly enriched.
source: Functional enrichment analysis of these cluster-defining marker genes identified those encoding immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domains as most significantly enriched (Figure 2A), including many cell adhesion molecules that are known to establish neuronal connectivity during development (Özkan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure and citation, describing the data analysis.

claim: Many members of the Immunoglobulin superfamily (IgSF) continue to be expressed in the adult and contribute to neuronal cluster identity.
source: Specifically, many members of the Immunoglobulin superfamily (IgSF) continue to be expressed in the adult and contribute to neuronal cluster identity (Figure 2B; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to figures, describing the data analysis.

claim: Dpr and DIP genes are markers for over 50% of neuronal clusters identified in the adult VNC.
source: The defective proboscis extension response (Dpr) subfamily, and their binding partners, the Dpr-interacting protein (DIP) subfamily, are markers for over 50% of neuronal clusters identified in the adult VNC (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing the data analysis.

claim: Dpr and DIP genes provide a complex interaction network regulating neural circuit assembly and have been proposed to act as neuronal 'identification tags' during development.
source: Dpr and DIP genes provide a complex interaction network regulating neural circuit assembly and have been proposed to act as neuronal 'identification tags' during development.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results.

claim: Distinct combinations of Dpr and DIP proteins are expressed by different neuronal classes in the developing optic lobe, the antennal lobe, and the VNC.
source: Distinct combinations of Dpr and DIP proteins are expressed by different neuronal classes in the developing optic lobe, the antennal lobe, and the VNC (Carrillo et al., 2015; Özkan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with citation support.

claim: Specific combinations of Beat and Side IgSF proteins play an important role in the sculpting the nervous system.
source: Specific combinations of Beat and Side IgSF proteins play an important role in the sculpting the nervous system (Özkan et al., 2013; Pipes et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with citation support.

claim: Almost all Beat and Side family members were found as cluster markers in the VNC.
source: Almost all Beat and Side family members were found as cluster markers in the VNC (Figure 2B), and their enrichment was largely mutually exclusive, with 80% of the identified clusters enriched for either Beats or Sides (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to figures, describing the data analysis.

claim: The enrichment of Beat and Side family members was largely mutually exclusive, with 80% of the identified clusters enriched for either Beats or Sides.
source: Almost all Beat and Side family members were found as cluster markers in the VNC (Figure 2B), and their enrichment was largely mutually exclusive, with 80% of the identified clusters enriched for either Beats or Sides (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to figures, describing the data analysis.

claim: The enrichment of IgSFs in the adult VNC supports their importance in establishing cell type specificity and suggests an ongoing role in maintenance of neuronal connectivity in the mature nervous system.
source: The enrichment of IgSFs in the adult VNC supports their importance in establishing cell type specificity and suggests an ongoing role in maintenance of neuronal connectivity in the mature nervous system (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing an inference from the data analysis.

claim: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) were significantly over-represented as cluster markers.
source: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) were also significantly over-represented as cluster markers (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to figures, describing the data analysis.

claim: GPCRs play a critical role in intercellular communication by interacting with a diverse group of extracellular ligands such as neurotransmitters, modulatory neuropeptides and biogenic amines, peptide hormones, and gases.
source: GPCRs play a critical role in intercellular communication by interacting with a diverse group of extracellular ligands such as neurotransmitters, modulatory neuropeptides and biogenic amines, peptide hormones, and gases (Hanlon and Andrew, 2015).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with citation support.

claim: A median of 8 GPCRs were expressed per cell and a median of 22 transmembrane receptors in total per cell.
source: We observed a median of 8 GPCRs expressed per cell and a median of 22 transmembrane receptors in total per cell.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results describing the data analysis.

claim: A median of 12 GPCRs were observed when considering the expression at the cluster level (with a threshold of 20% positive cells per cluster).
source: We saw a median of 12 GPCRs when we consider the expression at the cluster level (with a threshold of 20% positive cells per cluster; Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing the data analysis.

claim: Many GPCRs are significantly enriched in the individual clusters, but were, in general, expressed at low levels, in few cells per cluster, and across many clusters.
source: Although many GPCRs are significantly enriched in the individual clusters, they were, in general, expressed at low levels, in few cells per cluster, and across many clusters (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing the data analysis.

claim: The neuropeptide receptor family members had more inter-cluster variation in expression levels than the other GPCR subtypes, suggesting that they confer an added level of specialization.
source: The neuropeptide receptor family members had more inter-cluster variation in expression levels than the other GPCR subtypes, suggesting that they confer an added level of specialization.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results describing an inference from the data analysis.

claim: 80% of biogenic amine receptor family members are found as cluster markers.
source: We also saw that 80% of biogenic amine receptor family members, a diverse group of neurotransmitter receptors sensitive to biogenic amine neurotransmitters including dopamine, octopamine, serotonin and tyramine, are found as cluster markers (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results with reference to a figure, describing the data analysis.

claim: Odorant receptors, gustatory receptors, ionotropic receptors, and pickpocket sodium channels are predominantly found in first-order sensory neurons and in general, were not expressed in the VNC, as expected.
source: Odorant receptors, gustatory receptors, ionotropic receptors, and pickpocket sodium channels are predominantly found in first-order sensory neurons (Joseph and Carlson, 2015) and in general, were not expressed in the VNC, as expected.

claim: Or63a, Gr28b, Ir76a, ppk31 are all expressed in the VNC, albeit at low levels and in few cells.
source: There were exceptions, however, as Or63a, Gr28b, Ir76a, ppk31 are all expressed in the VNC, albeit at low levels and in few cells.

claim: Neurotransmitter-gated ion-channels were highly enriched as neuronal cluster markers, including 8 of the 10 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunits.
source: Neurotransmitter-gated ion-channels were also highly enriched as neuronal cluster markers (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 5, Figure 1—source data 1), including 8 of the 10 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunits (Littleton and Ganetzky, 2000).

claim: Over 20% of all Drosophila TFs were cluster markers in the adult VNC, the most enriched class of which was the homeodomain (HD) family.
source: Finally, over 20% of all Drosophila TFs were cluster markers in the adult VNC, the most enriched class of which was the homeodomain (HD) family (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 6).

source: We observed a median of 6 HD TFs per cell, and a median of 52 TFs in total per cell.

claim: Cluster expression of Iro-C genes appears to reflect the evolutionary history of the Iro-C.
source: Cluster expression of Iro-C genes appears to reflect this evolutionary history.
